source: VVOB Cambodia / MAFF Kampong Thom Provincial Department of Agriculture — IPM and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Rice, 9-point training presentation, presenter Mr. Tem Seng, Oct 5, 2010 (training slide deck; no elibrary URL visible)
text: Water should be supplied to match the rice plant's needs at each growth stage rather than kept at one constant depth throughout the season (ផ្តល់ទឹកគ្រប់គ្រាន់ តាមតម្រូវការតាមដំណាក់កាល). During the seedling/early establishment stage, keep water shallow, roughly 1-5 cm, so young plants are not overwhelmed. During the vegetative growth (tillering) stage, water can be maintained around 5 cm. The most water-sensitive stage is from panicle initiation through flowering, when the field should be kept with a good, steady water depth of at least 5-10 cm, since water shortage at this stage has the largest negative impact on grain formation and yield. This general staging is a useful guide, but exact depths should still be adjusted to local field conditions and water availability, note: this is a general good-practice guideline note that farmers should check current local extension guidance for field-specific decisions.
